# Library

```{r, echo=FALSE}
pkgs <- c("tidySEM", "ggplot2", "dplyr", "readr", "OpenMx", "knitr",
          "rempsyc", "papaja", "tidyr")

for (p in pkgs) {
  if (!require(p, character.only = TRUE)) {
    install.packages(p, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
    library(p, character.only = TRUE)
  }
}


```


# Load data

```{r}
df_1_without_id <- read.csv("../data/comp_modelling/session1_comp_params_anonymized.csv")

quests <- read.csv("../output/session1/questionnaire_scores.csv")

# Merge the questionnaires with the parameters dataframe
df_1_quests <- merge(
  df_1_without_id,
  quests,
  by = "subjID"
)

# Select only the relevant 5 parameters for the BCH analysis
df_1_quests <- df_1_quests %>%
  select(-rlwm_bias, -rlwm_decay, -rlwm_lapse, -rlwm_rho, -gng_alpha, -gng_lapse, -phys_beta, -phys_lapse)

# In order to reproduce the BCH analyses the order of the data matters. It needs to be in the same order as when the analysis was done
og_subjID_order <- read.csv("../data/session1/original_subjID_order.csv")

# Match the current data frame
df_1_quests <- df_1_quests[match(og_subjID_order$og_subjID, df_1_quests$subjID),]

# Z score normalization
df_1_without_id_z   <-  as.data.frame(scale(df_1_without_id))

data_lca_z<- df_1_without_id_z%>% select ( rlwm_alpha, gng_beta, gng_eps, foraging_exit_threshold, phys_k )

data_lca_z <- data_lca_z %>%
  rename(k = phys_k)




```

desc<- descriptives(data_lca_z)

"sd", "min", "max", "skew_2se", "kurt_2se")]

# Find best model
```{r}
#Fitting
fit_lca_z <- tidySEM::table_fit(lca_16_c_z)



#exluding models with sample <10%
fit_n_min01_z<-  fit_lca_z[ !(fit_lca_z$n_min < 0.1), ] 


#plotting fit
best_BIC_plot_z<- plot(fit_n_min01_z) + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, 
hjust = 1))   


#best model is 	free var 3, free var 4, free var, equal cov 3, 	free var, equal cov 4 all with WARNING
final_lca_model_z<- lca_16_c_z[["free var 3"]]

summary(final_lca_model_z)
print(final_lca_model_z)

# Testing the stability of the model with random starting point 
lca_try <- mxTryHard(
  final_lca_model_z,
  extraTries = 50,
  finetuneGradient = TRUE
)


summary(lca_try)

ll_final <- logLik(final_lca_model_z)

ll_try<- logLik(lca_try)  

#SAME LL: THE MODEL FIT IS STABLE

```

# FINAL MODEL
```{r}

# The best model
final_lca_model_z<- lca_16_c_z[["free var 3"]]

print(final_lca_model_z)

#Exploring warning
summary(lca_16_c_z[["free var 3"]])   # The 3-class free-variance model shows convergence problems.
                                    # OpenMx returned a RED status, indicating that the model did not satisfy
                                    # first-order optimality conditions and the optimizer could not improve
                                    # the solution during the final line search.
                                    # Parameter estimates may therefore be unreliable or unstable.



#Results
results_z<-table_results(final_lca_model_z) #  *** -> p < 0.001; ** -> p < 0.01 ; * -> p < 0.05

class_prob_z<- class_prob(final_lca_model_z)


class_comp <- data.frame(
  Label = results_z$label,
  Estimate = results_z$est_sig,
  ConfInt = results_z$confint,
  Class = results_z$class
  
)

class_comp<- class_comp [grep("Means",class_comp$Label), ]

results_z$pval
```

# Plotting results
```{r}
plot_bivariate_z<- plot_bivariate(final_lca_model_z)
print(plot_bivariate_z)



profiles_4c_z <- tidySEM::plot_profiles(final_lca_model_z)
str(profiles_4c_z$data)
#jpeg("prfiles_4c_z.jpg")
for(i in 1:length(profiles_4c_z$layers)){

  if("GeomPoint" %in% class(profiles_4c_z$layers[[i]]$geom)){

    profiles_4c_z$layers[[i]]$position <- position_jitterdodge(
      dodge.width = 0.8,
      jitter.width = 0.05
    )

  } else {

    profiles_4c_z$layers[[i]]$position <- position_dodge(width = 0.8)

  }
}

plot_label <- c("Profile 1: Low RL / High vigor", "Profile 2: Low RL / low vigor", "Profile 3: High RL / normal vigor")
p <- profiles_4c_z +


  labs(
    x = "Parameter",
    y = "Z-Score",
    color = "Profile",
    # fill = "Profile",
    shape = "Profile",
    linetype = "Profile"
  ) +

  scale_color_discrete(
    labels = plot_label
  ) +

  scale_fill_discrete(
    labels = plot_label
  ) +

  scale_shape_discrete(
    labels = plot_label
  ) +

  scale_linetype_discrete(
    labels = plot_label
  ) +

  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +

  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

print(p)



density_4c_z<-tidySEM::plot_density(final_lca_model_z)
print(density_4c_z)

#jpeg("density_4c_z.jpg")

## Adjustments for the manuscript
p <- profiles_4c_z +
      geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50", linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_x_discrete(
    limits = c("rlwm_alpha", "GNG Beta", "GNG Epsilon", "Foraging Exit Threshold", "Effort K"),
    labels = c("RLWM α", "GNG β", "GNG ε", "Foraging Exit Threshold", "Effort κ")
  ) +
  labs(x = "Parameter", y = "Z-Score", color = "Profile", shape = "Profile", linetype = "Profile") +
  scale_color_discrete(labels = plot_label) +
  scale_fill_discrete(labels = plot_label) +
  scale_shape_discrete(labels = plot_label) +
  scale_linetype_discrete(labels = plot_label) +

  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

# Save the figure used for the manuscript
ggsave("../output/session1/profiles_parameters.jpg", plot = p, width = 10, height = 6, dpi = 300)

```

# Diagnosis 

```{r}
post_class_prob<- class_prob(final_lca_model_z, type="individual")#each individual has a high posterior class probability for one class

est_freq <- class_prob(final_lca_model_z, type ="sum.posterior")#the estimated frequency table of the latent categorical variable. This table takes classification error into account, so individuals can contribute partially to multiple classes.

freq_table<- class_prob(final_lca_model_z, type ="sum.mostlikely")  #the frequency table of the variable M, FM, is obtained by running class_prob(res,” sum.mostlikely”). Unlike FP, FM ignores classification error.

avg_post_prob<- class_prob(final_lca_model_z, type ="avg.mostlikely") #the average posterior probabilities by most likely class membership. This table gives the column means of P for the k subsets of observations with most likely class of M¼1...k:Each row gives the mean probability of being assigned to each class for participants assigned to one particular class according to M. (>0.6)



```

#BCH Analyses Mania
```{r}

bch_model_z <- tidySEM::BCH(
    x = final_lca_model_z,
    model = "Score_ASRM ~ 1",
    data = df_1_quests 
)


sum_bch_z<- summary(bch_model_z)   #M=mean; S=Variance

#LRT


#NON Restricted model 



bch_nrest_fit_z <- OpenMx::mxRun(bch_model_z)



#LRT 1-2


vin_c1_c2_z <- OpenMx::mxConstraint(
  class1.M[1,1] == class2.M[1,1],
  name = "vin_c1_c2_z"
)

bch_rest_c1_c2 <- OpenMx::mxModel(bch_model_z, vin_c1_c2_z)

bch_rest_fit_c1_c2 <- mxRun(bch_rest_c1_c2)

LRT_c1_c2 <- mxCompare(bch_nrest_fit_z, bch_rest_fit_c1_c2)   #SIGNIFICANT 





#LRT 1-3

vin_c1_c3_z <- OpenMx::mxConstraint(
  class1.M[1,1] == class3.M[1,1],
  name = "vin_c1_c3_z"
)

bch_rest_c1_c3 <- OpenMx::mxModel(bch_model_z, vin_c1_c3_z)
bch_rest_fit_c1_c3 <- mxRun(bch_rest_c1_c3)

LRT_c1_c3 <- mxCompare(bch_nrest_fit_z, bch_rest_fit_c1_c3)  # SIGNIFICANT 

#LRT  2-3

vin_c2_c3_z <- OpenMx::mxConstraint(
  class2.M[1,1] == class3.M[1,1],
  name = "vin_c2_c3_z"
)

bch_rest_c2_c3 <- OpenMx::mxModel(bch_model_z, vin_c2_c3_z)
bch_rest_fit_c2_c3 <- mxRun(bch_rest_c2_c3)

LRT_c2_c3 <- mxCompare(bch_nrest_fit_z, bch_rest_fit_c2_c3)  #SIGNIFICANT 
```
